subject: Narrowing definition of valid wear time to a specific day segment

messages.author: 33a987d6141d8d65
messages.subject: Narrowing definition of valid wear time to a specific day segment
parts:
Hi Everyone, 


I wondered if it is possible to narrow the definition of a minimum required number of valid hours to a specific time segment during the day? I am using includedaycrit argument to specify the minimum number of hours of accelerometer wear within a 24-hour segment. Ideally, I would like to apply the minimum valid hours of wear criterion to a specific time segment (e.g. 8 am and 6:30 pm). Based on the arguments specified in part 2, it seems that it may not be easily done. 


Since I am new to GGIR and am still exploring different options, I wondered if other users may have experience in successfully narrowing the definition of valid wear time to a specific day segment, which they might be willing to share.


Thank you to all the users sharing their experiences and to colleagues who build and maintain this resource.


Best,


Dominika

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Narrowing definition of valid wear time to a specific day segment
parts:
part2_daysummary.csv gives you all the information you need to calculate your own part2_summary file, with time window specific inclusion criteria.
My general approach is to focus on day level estimates and provide a basic set of person level aggregates. If users want more person level aggregates then they can do it themselves.

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Narrowing definition of valid wear time to a specific day segment
parts:
I think I figured it out. I used ilevels in part 2 to specify physical activity thresholds which provided data on each intensity within the desired time windows. 
Thank you for clarifying that for "0-24" variables data from days with a minimum number of valid hours is used. 
Best,
Dominika
